name: Darts-clone
baseline: Darts (Double-ARray Trie System, original header library by Taku Kudo)
workload: Static double-array trie dictionaries built from 7 key sets (Japanese and English word lists, Wikipedia titles, Google unigram lists, 7-digit postal codes; 118k to 13.6M keys); average ns per key for exactMatchSearch(), commonPrefixSearch() and traverse(), keys queried in lexicographic and in random order, plus dictionary size and build time.
claimed_speedup: Random-order exactMatchSearch: JA1 170.4 vs 76.2 ns/key (about 2.2x faster, derived from page data), EN1 228.5 vs 111.3 ns/key (about 2.1x, derived from page data), EN3 545.3 vs 453.3 ns/key. Lexicographic exactMatchSearch: JA1 48.9 vs 33.1 ns/key. Dictionary size halved (JA1 7,023 KB vs 3,336 KB; EN2 513,873 KB vs 240,634 KB). Build time lower (JA1 828 vs 368 ns/key). Author attributes the speedup to better cache use from the smaller dictionary.
compiler_and_flags: gcc 4.3.3 (optimization flags not stated on the page); benchmark tool darts-benchmark ships with the repo
hardware: Dell Precision T3400, Core 2 Quad Q9550 2.83GHz, 64-bit Ubuntu 9.04
stars_or_usage: 161 stars; packaged as a vcpkg port (darts-clone)
tradeoffs: Static dictionary (no updates). Not a true succinct structure: it is a compact double-array trie (32-bit units, DAWG-merged), so it is far larger than LOUDS or MARISA tries (marisa-trie README lists 376,613,888 bytes for darts-clone against 50,753,560 for marisa-trie on 9.8M Wikipedia titles). Build time grows when every key has a unique value (JA2 5,942 ns/key). Dictionary files are not compatible with Darts.
caveats: Baseline is the original Darts, not SDSL or sux. Numbers are from a 2009-era machine and compiler, in a Japanese-language page; optimization flags are not stated. Results are mixed: on the postal-code set (DIG) Darts-clone is slower for exactMatchSearch (24.2 vs 18.8 ns/key lexicographic), and traverse() is slower on most word lists (for example JA2 144.6 vs 119.1 ns/key lexicographic). The page itself warns that search time depends heavily on cache sizes, inlining and key distribution. On the large Wikipedia and n-gram sets the random-order gain is smaller (JA2 516.4 vs 620.8 ns/key). Found as a registry hit, but it is a compact trie rather than a rank/select structure, so category fit is loose.
found_via: vcpkg port darts-clone (raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vcpkg/master/ports/darts-clone/vcpkg.json, version-string 1767ab87cffe, BSD-2-Clause), found by probing port names around succinct trie libraries; web search 'C++ succinct trie OR double-array trie faster than marisa-trie darts-clone benchmark github' also surfaced it; PyPI binding dartsclone 0.10.2 exists
